name: Bell pepper blossom-end rot
scientific_name: Physiological disorder caused by calcium deficiency in fruit tissues
symptoms: Small light green or yellow spot at the blossom end of the fruit Sunken dark brown or black lesion on fruit tip Fruit tissue collapse and dry rot Premature fruit ripening Black fungal growth (secondary Alternaria colonization) Secondary bacterial soft rot in severe cases
description: Blossom-end rot is a physiological disorder caused by a lack of calcium in developing fruits. It affects rapidly growing fruits when calcium supply to fruit tissue is insufficient. The disorder leads to tissue collapse at the blossom end of the fruit and can cause significant yield losses.
management: Maintain consistent soil moisture with proper irrigation Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization Improve soil structure for better root growth Use mulching to regulate soil moisture and temperature Monitor soil nutrient levels with soil testing
prevention: Ensure adequate calcium levels in soil Maintain regular irrigation schedules Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization Improve drainage and root health Use drip irrigation to stabilize water supply Avoid root damage from cultivation or diseases
